label: Art direction
description: Sets one visual reference and enforces it across the set.

label: Audio production
description: Mixes for speech intelligibility first and music second.

label: Comedy writing
description: Writes the setup plainly and puts the turn last.

label: Editing
description: Cuts filler, prefers concrete verbs, and keeps one idea per paragraph.

label: Game design
description: Tunes a core loop and its feedback before adding content.

label: Naming
description: Generates names that are short, sayable, and clear of collisions.

label: Poetry
description: Works in image and rhythm, and removes any line that only explains.

label: Scripting
description: Writes scenes that carry information through action and subtext.

label: Storytelling
description: Builds tension from a want and an obstacle, not from adjectives.

label: Worldbuilding
description: Keeps internal rules consistent and states them before bending them.

label: Analytical SQL
description: Writes window-function SQL and is explicit about grain and fan-out.

label: Applied ML
description: Starts from a baseline and refuses to add complexity without a measured gain.

label: Data visualisation
description: Picks the chart the question needs and labels axes so it reads without a caption.

label: dbt modelling
description: Builds staged, tested models with documented joins and freshness expectations.

label: ETL/ELT
description: Designs idempotent pipelines that can be re-run without duplicating rows.

label: Experiment analysis
description: Checks assignment balance, power and multiple comparisons before calling a winner.

label: Pandas
description: Reshapes data with vectorised operations and checks dtype assumptions first.

label: Statistics
description: Chooses tests from the data shape, reports effect sizes and uncertainty.

label: Warehouse modelling
description: Separates raw, staging and mart layers with clear ownership.

label: Accessibility
description: Covers focus order, labels, reduced motion and keyboard-only paths.

label: Colour & contrast
description: Builds accessible palettes and checks contrast against real surface colours.

label: Design systems
description: Extends an existing token and component system rather than inventing a parallel one.

label: Figma
description: Works in components, variants and auto-layout instead of ad-hoc frames.

label: Iconography
description: Keeps an icon set optically consistent at the sizes it ships at.

label: Motion
description: Uses motion for state change, with durations short enough to feel immediate.

label: Prototyping
description: Prototypes the smallest artefact that can be put in front of a user.

label: Responsive layout
description: Designs the narrow case first and names what collapses at each breakpoint.

label: Typography
description: Pairs type, sets a scale, and fixes measure and line-height before colour.

label: UX research
description: Plans interviews and usability tests that answer a decision, not a curiosity.

label: Assessment
description: Writes items that test understanding, not recall of phrasing.

label: Curriculum design
description: Sequences outcomes so each unit depends on the last one.

label: Feedback
description: Gives feedback on the work against the goal, with one next step.

label: Learning accessibility
description: Provides multiple representations and removes time pressure where it adds nothing.

label: Learning science
description: Applies retrieval practice and spacing instead of re-reading.

label: Lesson planning
description: Plans around one learning objective and its misconception.

label: Scaffolding
description: Adds support that is withdrawn as competence grows.

label: Tutoring
description: Diagnoses the gap before explaining, and checks understanding after.

label: API design
description: Shapes request/response contracts, versioning and error envelopes that stay stable.

label: App security
description: Threat-models input, auth and secrets handling; flags injection and privilege paths.

label: CI/CD
description: Builds pipelines that fail fast, cache well and never leak credentials into logs.

label: Code review
description: Reviews for correctness, naming and blast radius — and says which comments block.

label: Containers
description: Writes reproducible Dockerfiles and keeps images small and cache-friendly.

label: CSS & layout
description: Handles layout with flexbox and grid, tokenised spacing, and responsive breakpoints.

label: Go
description: Idiomatic Go: explicit errors, context propagation, and goroutines with bounded lifetimes.

label: Kubernetes
description: Reasons about probes, resources, rollout strategy and failure domains.

label: Node.js services
description: Writes small HTTP services, middleware chains and graceful shutdown handling.

label: Observability
description: Adds structured logs, metrics and traces that answer a specific operational question.

label: Performance
description: Profiles before optimising, then measures the delta in numbers.

label: Python
description: Writes typed, tested Python with clear module seams and no hidden global state.

label: React
description: Builds composable components with correct hook dependencies and explicit loading/empty/error states.

label: Refactoring
description: Splits seams and shrinks diffs without changing observable behaviour.

label: Rust
description: Ownership-aware Rust, preferring clear lifetimes over clones.

label: SQL
description: Writes readable queries and understands indexes, joins and query plans.

label: Testing
description: Writes tests that fail for the right reason, at the cheapest layer that can catch the bug.

label: TypeScript
description: Reads and writes strict TypeScript, including generics, narrowing and module boundaries.

label: AP/AR operations
description: Keeps cash timing visible and flags anything aging past terms.

label: Budgeting
description: Builds a budget from drivers and shows what happens when they move.

label: Financial modelling
description: Builds models where every assumption is a labelled input, never a hard-coded cell.

label: Financial reporting
description: Produces statements that tie out, with the reconciliation shown.

label: Forecasting
description: Present three scenarios with the assumption that separates them.

label: Unit economics
description: Computes contribution margin per unit and states which costs are excluded.

label: Valuation
description: Shows the comparable set and the sensitivity around the chosen multiple.

label: Variance analysis
description: Explains the gap by driver, and distinguishes timing from permanent delta.

label: Care coordination
description: Keeps handovers and follow-ups from falling between providers.

label: Clinical documentation
description: Documents facts, timestamps and decisions without editorialising.

label: Health compliance
description: Handles sensitive data under the minimum-necessary principle.

label: Intake
description: Collects a structured history and flags anything needing escalation.

label: Patient education
description: Explains in plain language and checks understanding back.

label: Safety boundaries
description: Recognises when to stop advising and route to a clinician.

label: Triage support
description: Routes by red-flag symptoms and declines to guess at a diagnosis.

label: Wellness coaching
description: Sets habits small enough to survive a bad week.

label: Compliance
description: Turns an obligation into an owner, a control and a review cadence.

label: Contract review
description: Summarises obligations, term and termination before line-level comments.

label: IP & licensing
description: Checks licence compatibility and ownership before reuse.

label: Policy drafting
description: Writes policy with an explicit scope and a named exception path.

label: Privacy
description: Maps data flows to a lawful basis and flags anything retained without one.

label: Redlining
description: Proposes minimal alternative language with the risk explained.

label: Risk assessment
description: Rates likelihood against impact and names the mitigation and residual risk.

label: Terms & policies
description: Writes terms a normal user could read, without hiding the material limits.

label: Brand voice
description: Keeps a consistent register across surfaces and names what the brand will not say.

label: Content strategy
description: Plans a content set that answers a journey rather than a keyword list.

label: Copywriting
description: Leads with the concrete benefit and cuts every hedge word.

label: Email marketing
description: Writes subject lines that survive a crowded inbox and one clear CTA.

label: Marketing analytics
description: Attributes conversions honestly and separates correlation from incrementality.

label: Paid acquisition
description: Structures campaigns around one testable variable at a time.

label: SEO
description: Maps intent to pages, fixes structure before copy, and avoids keyword stuffing.

label: Social media
description: Adapts one idea per platform instead of cross-posting the same text.

label: Incident response
description: Runs the response, keeps a timeline, and writes the blameless follow-up.

label: Inventory
description: Sets reorder points from lead time and demand spread.

label: Logistics
description: Plans capacity against demand variability, not the average.

label: OKRs
description: Writes key results as measurable outcomes rather than activity lists.

label: Process mapping
description: Draws the current state honestly, including the workarounds.

label: Project management
description: Keeps dependencies and the critical path explicit and current.

label: Vendor management
description: Reviews vendors on reliability and exit cost, not only price.

label: Workflow automation
description: Automates the stable, high-frequency step and leaves the judgement call manual.

label: Compensation
description: Benchmarks against a stated market and explains the band.

label: Engagement
description: Reads survey results by team and separates signal from sample noise.

label: HR policy
description: Writes policy that is consistent across regions and actually enforceable.

label: Interviewing
description: Asks questions with a scoring rubric agreed before the call.

label: Onboarding
description: Sequences the first two weeks so a new hire can ship something small.

label: Org design
description: Designs reporting lines around decisions, not around people.

label: Performance management
description: Gives feedback tied to observed behaviour and a specific next action.

label: Sourcing
description: Writes outreach that names the specific work, not the company perks.

label: Competitive analysis
description: Compares on the axis users switch on, not on feature checklists.

label: Discovery
description: Separates the problem being solved from the feature being requested.

label: Experimentation
description: Sizes the effect an experiment must detect before it is worth running.

label: Prioritisation
description: Applies a stated scoring rule and shows the trade-off it forces.

label: Product metrics
description: Defines one primary metric, its guardrails, and how it could be gamed.

label: Roadmapping
description: Sequences work by risk and learning value, not by who shouted loudest.

label: Spec writing
description: Writes specs short enough to be read, with the open questions still visible.

label: User stories
description: Writes stories with testable acceptance criteria and an explicit non-goal.

label: Citation
description: Cites to the specific page or dataset, never to "a study".

label: Competitive intelligence
description: Tracks competitor changes from public signals and timestamps each finding.

label: Fact-checking
description: Traces a claim to its origin and flags where a summary drifted from the source.

label: Literature search
description: Builds a search strategy and records what was excluded, not just what was found.

label: Research interviews
description: Asks about past behaviour instead of hypothetical future intent.

label: Source evaluation
description: Weighs primary over secondary sources and states the confidence level.

label: Survey design
description: Writes neutral, single-barrelled questions and pilots before fielding.

label: Synthesis
description: Collapses many sources into claims, with the disagreement left visible.

label: CRM hygiene
description: Keeps stages and next-action dates accurate enough to forecast from.

label: Customer onboarding
description: Hands off with context so the customer never repeats themselves.

label: Discovery calls
description: Runs a call that ends with a next step agreed by both sides.

label: Forecasting
description: Separates committed, best-case and pipeline with stated assumptions.

label: Negotiation
description: Trades on value and terms rather than discounting price by reflex.

label: Objection handling
description: Treats an objection as missing information and answers it without pressure.

label: Proposals
description: Writes proposals where scope, price and exclusions are unambiguous.

label: Prospecting
description: Qualifies against a written ideal-customer profile before reaching out.

label: Escalation
description: Escalates with reproduction steps and a clear ask, not a forwarded thread.

label: Help documentation
description: Writes steps a first-time user can follow without prior context.

label: Response macros
description: Keeps canned replies specific enough to feel written for one person.

label: Root-cause analysis
description: Separates the trigger from the underlying condition before proposing a fix.

label: SLA management
description: Tracks first-response and resolution clocks and flags the ones about to breach.

label: Support tone
description: Stays plain and accountable, and never blames the user or the tool.

label: Ticket triage
description: Classifies by impact and urgency, and routes before replying.

label: Troubleshooting
description: Asks for the one datum that splits the hypothesis space, not a screenshot dump.
